questions.prompt: How does working memory differ from sustained attention?
questions.answer: Working memory retains/manipulates task information; sustained attention maintains engagement with a task goal.
questions.feedback: Describe a task that needs both.

questions.prompt: Why is a memory-capacity estimate not a universal concentration timer?
questions.answer: Memory experiments measure performance under specific conditions, not a fixed duration of focus.
questions.feedback: Distinguish number of items from elapsed time.

questions.answer: It externalises some memory demands and can help maintain the task rule.
questions.feedback: Do not equate aid use with incompetence.

questions.prompt: Why can the worked comparison not isolate the benefit of the table?
questions.answer: It changed two factors and the trial order may matter.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only. Use answer-specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Distinguishes three attentional demands, identifies a task-specific support and interprets a comparison without diagnosing ability.
scoring.transfer: Create an attention-demand map for a novel fictional task such as comparing three supplier quotes. Identify two competing demands, one external support and a meaningful quality measure. Explain why the support suits the task, and design a fairer follow-up comparison.
scoring.pass: All four mapped course criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety boundaries. Quiz score alone cannot certify competency.
